prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

You are reviewing layouts of one table, all rendered in a real browser with identical content, font, padding and colours; only column widths differ. You do not know who or what produced them. The first image is the content overview (every cell on one line).
Table: Solar PV capacity additions by country and quarter, 2024 (MW) (language en).
Grid: 9 columns × 8 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Merged cells: "Segment" spans 1 col × 3 row; "Europe" spans 4 col × 1 row; "Asia-Pacific" spans 4 col × 1 row; "Germany" spans 2 col × 1 row; "France" spans 2 col × 1 row; "Japan" spans 2 col × 1 row; "Australia" spans 2 col × 1 row.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Segment" · longest unbreakable word 86px · one-line width 172px
  col 2: header "Europe › Germany › Q1" · longest unbreakable word 40px · one-line width 40px
  col 3: header "Europe › Germany › Q2" · longest unbreakable word 40px · one-line width 40px
  col 4: header "Europe › France › Q1" · longest unbreakable word 33px · one-line width 33px
  col 5: header "Europe › France › Q2" · longest unbreakable word 38px · one-line width 38px
  col 6: header "Asia-Pacific › Japan › Q1" · longest unbreakable word 38px · one-line width 38px
  col 7: header "Asia-Pacific › Japan › Q2" · longest unbreakable word 38px · one-line width 38px
  col 8: header "Asia-Pacific › Australia › Q1" · longest unbreakable word 28px · one-line width 28px
  col 9: header "Asia-Pacific › Australia › Q2" · longest unbreakable word 38px · one-line width 38px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
This table cannot fit without splitting words at 360px. You MAY choose a total wider than 359px (the reader then scrolls horizontally), or squeeze and accept splits — a design decision.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Rate EACH layout independently: "excellent" | "good" | "acceptable" | "poor" | "bad", with a short reason that points at what you see. Then name the best layout(s) (ties allowed), say how confident you are (low/medium/high), and note anything you are unsure about.
